title: Logiks Plugin MCP Tools Manifest
description: Sits alongside a plugin's logiks.json (same directory). Declares the MCP tools a plugin exposes. The Worker aggregates every installed plugin's tools.json and reports them to the AppServer at registration (system.registerWorker), the same way it already reports `policies` and `navigation`. The AppServer's MCP registry (api/controllers/mcp/registry.js) turns each entry into a callable MCP tool.

namespace.description: Short, stable slug for this plugin's tools. Prefixed onto every tool name (`${namespace}__${name}`) so two plugins can't collide in the global MCP tool list. Pick something that won't change - renaming it changes every tool's public name.

plugin.description: Must match this plugin's logiks.json `package` (or `marketid`), so a tool can be traced back to the plugin that owns it.

version.description: Manifest version, independent of the plugin's own version. Bump when tool signatures change.

name.description: Combined with the manifest's `namespace` as `${namespace}__${name}`. Keep the combined length <= 64 chars - that's OpenAI's tool-name limit, and Claude/other MCP hosts follow the same convention.

description.description: Shown to the calling LLM verbatim. State what the tool does and when to use it - this is the only thing the model uses to decide whether to call it.

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema (type: object) describing this tool's arguments. Passed through to MCP clients as-is, so keep it self-contained (no external $refs).

action.description: A Moleculer broker action already exposed by this plugin's Worker service, e.g. 'demo.lookupCustomer'. Invoked as ctx.call(action, args, {meta: ctx.meta}) - the action owns its own DB access, validation, and read/write semantics. Not a file path or inline function: the tool must already exist as a normal service action.

policy.description: A policy key from this plugin's logiks.json `policies` map (e.g. 'demo.allow.access'). If set, the call is gated through RBAC.checkPolicy(ctx, policy, false) before the action runs. Omit for tools any authenticated MCP caller may use.

readOnly.description: Advisory hint surfaced to MCP clients - some hosts use it to decide whether to ask the user to confirm before calling. Does not change server-side behavior; the action itself is still responsible for enforcing read-only semantics.
